content: 1. Before starting treatment, confirm the pregnancy status of females of reproductive potential. 2. Safety and efficacy of the drug have not been established in premenarchal patients. 3. Ibrexafungerp increases the levels or effects of elacestrant by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 4. Ibrexafungerp increases the levels or effects of etrasimod. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Increased exposure to etrasimod is expected in patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers when coadministered with moderate to strong CYP2C8 inhibitors. 5. Ibrexafungerp increases the levels or effects of nirogacestat by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Ibrexafungerp increases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 100 mg/day and monitor closely for adverse effects. If adverse effects occur, further reduce the dose to 50 mg/day. 7. Ibrexafungerp increases the levels or effects of pacritinib by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 8. Ibrexafungerp increases the levels or effects of repotrectinib by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Discontinue strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors and wait 3-5 elimination half-lives before initiating repotrectinib. 9. Ibrexafungerp increases the levels or effects of tovorafenib by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of tovorafenib (a CYP2C8 substrate) with strong or moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors. 10. Ibrexafungerp increases the levels or effects of atogepant by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Ibrexafungerp increases the levels or effects of capivasertib by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the capivasertib dose if coadministered with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 12. Ibrexafungerp increases the levels or effects of daprodustat. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors increase daprodustat exposure. If coadministered with moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors, reduce the daprodustat starting dose by half (except if the starting dose is already 1 mg). Monitor hemoglobin and adjust the daprodustat dose when initiating or stopping therapy with moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors during treatment. 13. Ibrexafungerp increases the levels or effects of daridorexant by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. The daridorexant dose should not exceed 25 mg per night when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 14. Ibrexafungerp increases the levels or effects of finerenone by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustment of either finerenone or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust finerenone dosage as needed. 15. Ibrexafungerp increases the levels or effects of gepirone by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the gepirone dose by 50% when used concomitantly with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 16. Ibrexafungerp increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Ibrexafungerp increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the lumateperone dose to 21 mg/day if coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 18. Ibrexafungerp increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Initiation of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may require a decreased mavacamten dose. 19. Ibrexafungerp increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor for mavorixafor adverse effects if coadministered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. If necessary, reduce the mavorixafor daily dose. 20. Ibrexafungerp increases the levels or effects of norgestrel by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic concentrations of norgestrel, which may increase the risk of adverse effects. 21. Ibrexafungerp increases the levels or effects of palovarotene by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid coadministration of palovarotene, a CYP3A substrate, with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palovarotene dose by 50%. 22. Ibrexafungerp increases the levels or effects of resmetirom. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the dose of resmetirom (a CYP2C8 substrate) with moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors. 23. Ibrexafungerp increases levels of seladelpar by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Exercise caution in patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers taking seladelpar and are coadministered a moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 24. Ibrexafungerp increases the levels or effects of sparsentan by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment is needed. Monitor blood pressure, serum potassium, edema, and kidney function regularly if sparsentan is coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 25. Ibrexafungerp increases the levels or effects of vardenafil by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. The vardenafil dose may need to be reduced if coadministered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 26. Ibrexafungerp and voclosporin may increase each other’s toxicity through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Coadministration with drugs associated with nephrotoxicity may increase the risk for acute and/or chronic nephrotoxicity. 27. Ibrexafungerp increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce zanubrutinib (a CYP3A4 substrate) to 80 mg PO BID when coadministered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. Interrupt the dose as recommended for adverse reactions. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor, resume the previous dose of zanubrutinib. 28. Ibrexafungerp is contraindicated during pregnancy due to potential fetal harm based on animal data. Verify pregnancy status before initiating treatment in females of reproductive potential. Reassess pregnancy status prior to each dose when used monthly for six months to reduce the incidence of recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis (RVVC). If inadvertently administered during pregnancy or if pregnancy is detected within four days after receiving therapy, report the pregnancy to SCYNEXIS, Inc. at 1-888-982-SCYX (7299). 29. There is no data on the presence of ibrexafungerp in human or animal milk, its effects on breastfed infants, or its effects on milk production. 30. Ibrexafungerp is a triterpenoid antifungal agent that inhibits glucan synthase, an enzyme involved in the formation of 1,3-beta-D-glucan, an essential component of the fungal cell wall. It exhibits concentration-dependent fungicidal activity against Candida species as measured by time-kill studies. 31. Ibrexafungerp is primarily metabolized by hydroxylation via CYP3A4, followed by glucuronidation and sulfation of an inactive hydroxylated metabolite. 32. The half-life of ibrexafungerp is approximately 20 hours. 33. Excretion occurs primarily through feces (90%, with 51% unchanged) and urine (1%). 34. Ibrexafungerp can be taken with or without food. 35. Tablets should be stored at 20-25°C (68-77°F), with excursions permitted to 15-30°C (59-86°F).
